```{r}
main_data_self <- readRDS("data/processed/main_data_self.rds")
main_data_official <- readRDS("data/processed/main_data_official.rds")
extended_data_self <- readRDS("data/processed/extended_data_self.rds")
extended_data_official <- readRDS("data/processed/extended_data_official.rds")
```

```{r}
datasets <- list(
  main_data_self = main_data_self,
  main_data_official = main_data_official,
  extended_data_self = extended_data_self,
  extended_data_official = extended_data_official
)

overview <- bind_rows(lapply(names(datasets), function(nm) {
  df <- datasets[[nm]]

  data.frame(
    dataset = nm,
    observations = nrow(df),
    variables = ncol(df),
    start = min(df$date),
    end = max(df$date),
    missing = sum(is.na(df))
  )
}))

print(overview)
```

```{r}
missing_count <- colSums(is.na(extended_data_self))
missing_count[missing_count > 0]
```

```{r}
missing_count <- colSums(is.na(extended_data_official))
missing_count[missing_count > 0]
```

```{r}
print ("Row and Col positions of NA values")
which(is.na(extended_data_official$US_ACOGNO), arr.ind=TRUE)

print ("Row and Col positions of NA values")
which(is.na(extended_data_self$US_ACOGNO), arr.ind=TRUE)
```

`US_ACOGNO` missing values are from 1981-01-01 to 1992-01-01. From 1992-02-01 onwards, there is data for `US_ACOGNO`, except for 2026-07-01. The disparity in missing values for official and self data is from this variable (difference = 132). 

## Compare self-adjusted seasonality and officially adjusted main_data

```{r}
inflation_compare <- main_data_self %>%
  select(date, inflation_self = inflation_mom) %>%
  inner_join(
    main_data_official %>%
      select(date, inflation_official = inflation_mom),
    by = "date"
  ) %>%
  filter(date <= cutoff)

inflation_compare %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -date,
    names_to = "series",
    values_to = "inflation"
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(date, inflation * 100, color = series)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.5, alpha = 0.8) +
  labs(
    title = "Canadian Monthly Inflation: Self vs Official",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Monthly Log Inflation (%)",
    color = "CPI Adjustment"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Descriptive statistics for inflation

```{r}
# descriptive statistics 
inflation_stats <- inflation_compare %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -date,
    names_to = "series",
    values_to = "inflation"
  ) %>%
  group_by(series) %>%
  summarise(
    mean = mean(inflation, na.rm = TRUE),
    median = median(inflation, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(inflation, na.rm = TRUE),
    min = min(inflation, na.rm = TRUE),
    max = max(inflation, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(inflation_stats)
```

We plot autocorrelation and partial autocorrelation to examine our inflation variables. 

```{r}
# comparing across same time periods (starting from 1992)
start_date <- as.Date("1992-01-01")
end_date <- as.Date("2019-12-01")

self_common <- main_data_self %>%
  filter(date >= start_date, date <= end_date)

official_common <- main_data_official %>%
  filter(date >= start_date, date <= end_date)

inflation_common <- main_data_self %>%
  select(date, self = inflation_mom) %>%
  inner_join(
    main_data_official %>%
      select(date, official = inflation_mom),
    by = "date"
  ) %>%
  filter(
    date <= end_date,
    complete.cases(self, official)
  )

par(mfrow = c(2, 2))

acf(inflation_common$self, lag.max = 36,
    main = "ACF: Self-adjusted")

pacf(inflation_common$self, lag.max = 36,
     main = "PACF: Self-adjusted")

acf(inflation_common$official, lag.max = 36,
    main = "ACF: Official")

pacf(inflation_common$official, lag.max = 36,
     main = "PACF: Official")
```

Interpretation: 
- similar autocorrelation structures between self-adjusted and official CPI 
- both exhibit weak overall autocorrelation with a large negative correlation at lag 12 and a few isolated PACF spikes 
- Implications
  - supprts AR models, but AR(1) is not necessarily sufficient -- should use BIC or validation to choose best model, similar to Mederios et al. methodology 
  - similarity strengthens our confidence in self-adjusted CPI 

## Rolling volatility 
Does inflation volatility change across economic periods? 

```{r}
volatility_self <- main_data_self %>%
  arrange(date) %>%
  mutate(
    rolling_sd_12 = zoo::rollapply(
      inflation_mom,
      width = 12,
      FUN = sd,
      fill = NA,
      align = "right"
    )
  )

ggplot(volatility_self, aes(date, rolling_sd_12 * 100)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    title = "12-Month Rolling Volatility of Canadian Inflation (Self-adjusted CPI)",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Rolling SD (monthly percentage points)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
volatility_self <- main_data_official %>%
  arrange(date) %>%
  mutate(
    rolling_sd_12 = zoo::rollapply(
      inflation_mom,
      width = 12,
      FUN = sd,
      fill = NA,
      align = "right"
    )
  )

ggplot(volatility_self, aes(date, rolling_sd_12 * 100)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    title = "12-Month Rolling Volatility of Canadian Inflation (Officially-adjusted CPI)",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Rolling SD (monthly percentage points)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
